title: Four Sources of Happiness
paragraphs: Though not as mammoth as a mountain, the required yield from the paddy fields to one’s heart’s content, the ripeness of mind acquired through learning, the communion of the hearts of men, the villagers assembling to dance and sing together in rapture-this is happiness earned to one’s own heart’s fill rather than the sadistic pleasure derived from others’ misery. This happiness manifests itself in all its serenity on the day of Taip Poṅkal which the Tamiḻs celebrate as a day of happiness with lots of emotions. The following musical verse captures the sentiment above:
Hail Poṅkal, hail Poṅkal! Poṅkal which exudes mirth everywhere.
Hail Poṅkal, hail Poṅkal Toiling gods of folks! Tens of thousands of people you prop up.
The world has placed the crown upon your head - Your roar of resolution can dwarf even the peaks of the Himalayas.
Let us all speak of the greatness of the peasants, And wish them for their prosperity!
We shall shout, “Let milk (pāl) overflow!” That Pāl is the one Vaḷḷuvar has gifted us— The Pāls of Aṟam, Poruḷ and Kāmam. What more do we need?
Let’s cleanse our homes, cows, calves and get rid of dust and dirt. This is the real Bhogi!
Let’s uproot superstitious beliefs and remove their stench, Chisel our grey cells and rational thinking and gather knowledge. Let’s twist our moustaches And work for the empowerment of our womenfolk.
Let our women’s lips wear buds of smile - The women who love turmeric, ginger and sugar cane lofty And lands fertile!
Bull-fight for our youth was a child’s play then. Righteousness and fair-play are essential in public life. The joy of such a new life will cross the boundaries of the earth. Hail Poṅkal!
> The four sources of unmixed joy are > Riches, mind’s might, sexual union and play.
